title: Next: The Trip Point
summary: Closing splash celebrates local resilience only long enough to ask the harder question: the network may survive losing hardware, but can it survive a bad decision inside the circle of trust?
panelPlan: Full-page closing splash at a community water site after dark. A local mechanical/status indicator remains visibly active beneath an empty sky where an orbital path has gone dark.
Use one intact physical limit marker or capped gauge as the visual anchor. The image should say the local system is still holding without depicting any later failure.
Introduce subtle human proximity to the controls—hands, keys or access hardware—but do not show anyone defeating a limit, a damaged pump, or any specific Issue 4 event.
Typography should pivot sharply at THAT IS EXCELLENT NEWS, then leave the final question isolated before NEXT: THE TRIP POINT.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Public Sky just proved it can keep working after losing one of the things that made it possible.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Because the next thing that tests the system may not come from Tethergrid.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A network can survive a lost machine.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Can it survive a bad decision made by someone it trusts?

directionInline.text: Non-diegetic closing teaser. Preserve exact caption text. It may use the just-completed Glass Basin result, but it must not reveal who makes the next bad decision, what shortcut exists, what equipment is damaged, or how Issue 4 responds.
